entities.summary:
The Battle of Hormozdgan was a pivotal clash between the Parthian and Sasanian dynasties that took place on April 28, 224 AD, in Shushtar, marking the beginning of the Sasanian Empire's rise to power. This battle was a crucial turning point in the pre-Islamic history of the region, as it saw the Parthian Empire, which had long dominated the region, being overthrown by the Sasanian dynasty. The Sasanian Empire would go on to become one of the most powerful and influential empires in the ancient world, leaving a lasting legacy in the fields of art, architecture, and literature.

The Battle of Hormozdgan was a brutal and bloody conflict that saw the Parthian Empire's forces, led by the last Parthian king, Artabanus V, being defeated by the Sasanian Empire's forces, led by Ardashir I. The battle was a decisive victory for the Sasanians, who would go on to establish a new capital at Ctesiphon and bring about a period of relative stability and prosperity to the region. The battle also saw the introduction of new military tactics and technologies, such as the use of cavalry and siege engines, which would become characteristic of the Sasanian Empire's military prowess.

The legacy of the Battle of Hormozdgan can be seen in the rise of the Sasanian Empire, which would go on to have a profound impact on the development of the region. The Sasanian Empire's influence can be seen in the art, architecture, and literature of the time, and its legacy can still be seen in the modern-day cultures of the region. The battle also marked the beginning of a new era of conflict in the region, as the Sasanian Empire would go on to engage in a series of wars with the Roman Empire, which would have far-reaching consequences for the region.

In the words of the Sasanian historian, Khosrov, 'The Battle of Hormozdgan was a triumph of the Sasanian Empire, which marked the beginning of a new era of glory and prosperity in the region.'
